docs.title: ActTrader Dealer Manual
docs.text:
The ActTrader Dealer app is the dealing-desk side of ActTrader. From one window you see every client account, every pending order and every open position in your book. You can confirm or reject orders, manage positions for clients, and set prices and negotiation for each instrument.

Each page explains one part of the app and has a short video that shows it. The All Videos page lists every video and lets you search what is said in them.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Actions in the dealer app are real

Almost everything in this app changes a real client's account or affects every trader:

  • Market Open (top right) closes trading for every trader when you click it.
  • Change Price, instrument negotiation and dealer range apply to everyone who trades that instrument.
  • Close, Hedge and Close All Positions act on clients' money at once.
  • Send Message to All or Online reaches every trader.

When you are learning, open a window and press Cancel. Try real actions only on a test account.

docs.title: What is where
docs.text: Tab What it is for Page Accounts Every client account, and the Summary of positions under it Accounts Rates & Charts Instruments, live prices, Change Price, negotiation, range, charts Rates & Charts Orders Pending orders of all traders, orders waiting for you Pending Orders Trades Every open position in the book Open Positions Blotter Deals done today or this shift, M2M views Blotter Position History, Events and Message, Symbol Exposure Closed positions, server events and alerts, net exposure Events, History and Exposure

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
The Accounts tab lists every client account in your book.

Watch how: Work with client accounts (1:00)

docs.title: Reading the grid
docs.text:
Each row is one account: currency, account type (AcT), trader, Balance, Equity, used and usable margin (UsdMrgn, UsblMrgn), equity level, margin call (MC), open positions (OP), Net P/L, default amount (DA), negotiation mode (Neg) and dealer range (DR). Profit and equity update live with prices.

The DEALER row at the top is your own side of all client positions: the mirror of the whole book.

docs.title: Finding an account
docs.text: Type in the search box above the grid. It matches the account number, the trader or the account name. Clear the search (✕) to see every account again.

docs.title: The Summary of one account
docs.text: Select an account and the Summary panel under the grid shows only that account's positions, by instrument. Select the DEALER row, or nothing, for the whole book. See The Summary Panel.

docs.title: The account menu
docs.text:
Right-click an account for everything you can do with it.

Item What it does Set Negotiation, Set Default Amount (DA), Set Group, Set Dealer Range Change the account's settings. See Account Settings. Get Trader's Account(s) Show all accounts of this account's trader. Deactivate Account Stop the client from trading until you activate the account again. Reset Margin Call Clear a margin call on the account. Closed Positions Open Position History filtered to this account. The title shows the account; Show All Accounts goes back to everyone. Account Statement, MC Rates, Rollover Rates Open the reports for this account. Show in Trader Details window One window with the trader's accounts, positions and orders. Show All Managed, Show Banking, Show Clearing Which kinds of account the grid lists. Send Message… Write to this account. See Messages to Clients. Export data to CSV Save the grid as a spreadsheet file. Refresh Reload the accounts (F5).

docs.title: Messages to Clients
docs.text:
Send Message writes to clients from the dealing desk.

Watch how: Send a message to a client (0:39)

Open it in either of two ways:

  • Right-click an account in Accounts (or a row in Trades) and choose Send Message…. The window opens addressed to that account.
  • Click Message at the top right, to choose who it goes to.

Send to:

Option Who receives it All Every client. Online Every client logged in right now. Login One trader login, which you type in. Account One account, which you type in.

Type the message and press Send (or Ctrl+Enter). The window closes when the server confirms the message was sent.

All and Online reach every trader

Check the Send to choice before you press Send.

docs.title: Account Settings
docs.text:
Right-click an account in Accounts to change how the dealing desk treats it.

Watch how: Change an account's settings (1:39)

These are real changes to a client's account

Each setting takes effect for the client as soon as you press Ok.

docs.title: Set Negotiation
docs.text:
Decides which of the client's orders need your confirmation:

Mode Meaning Instrument Neg. Use the instrument's own negotiation setting (the usual choice). Zero Neg. Orders fill at once, with no dealer confirmation. Value Neg. Orders above a lot threshold need your confirmation. Complete Neg. Every order needs your confirmation.

The Neg column shows the account's mode.

docs.title: Set Default Amount (DA)
docs.text: The client's default trade size, either in trade steps or as a percentage of usable margin. The DA column shows it.

docs.title: Set Group
docs.text: A free-text label for grouping accounts in the grid. Leave it empty to clear it.

docs.title: Set Dealer Range
docs.text: The price tolerance for this client's orders. With Default system value ticked the account uses the system's range; untick it to set the account's own range. The DR column shows an account-specific range.

docs.title: Deactivate Account
docs.text: Stops the client from trading until you activate the account again.

docs.title: The Summary Panel
docs.text:
The Summary under the Accounts grid totals open positions by instrument and side.

Watch how: Read the Summary panel (1:08)

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column Meaning Lot Total lots for the instrument and side. NH Lot The lots that are not hedged. B/S Side of the book. The dealer's summary is the house side: the mirror of the clients' positions. AvOpen, AvClose, AvBEP Average open price, current close price, average break-even price. P/L Profit in points (pips × lots). Net P/L Profit in money, including charges, in the totals currency. NH P/L, NH Net P/L The same for the not-hedged part only. Instrum P/L The instrument's net result. Close (✕) Closes all positions in that row, for every client.

The ✕ in Close and Close All Positions act on every client at once

They close the clients' real positions. Use them only when you mean to.

docs.title: Scope and period
docs.text:
Right-click the Summary's column header to choose what it adds up. The title above the table always says what you are looking at, with the total net profit.

Menu item Shows Overall Summary All open positions. Day Summary Only positions opened today. Shift Summary Only positions opened in the current shift. Summary by All accounts Every client account (traders, groups and clearing). Summary by Selected accounts Only the accounts you select in the grid. Summary by Internal Trading Client accounts without the clearing accounts: your exposure to client trading. Not hedged summary only (NH Mode) Only what is not hedged.

docs.title: Other actions
docs.text:
• Right-click a row for View on Chart, Close All Positions and Export data to CSV.
  • Export CSV at the top right saves the table as a spreadsheet file.

docs.title: Blotter
docs.text:
The Blotter tab shows the deals done in the book and your result by instrument.

Watch how: Use the blotter (1:05)

docs.title: Views
docs.text: View What it shows Transaction Blotter Every deal: account, order, ticket, trader, instrument, lot, side and rate, with the time. Reopened (Trading) Positions carried over from earlier days, on the trading side. Reopened (Clearing) The same for the clearing side. Trading M2M The book marked to market: offset and market-maker profit for each instrument, with the total on top. Clearing M2M The same for the clearing side. Overall Info Both sides added up per instrument.

docs.title: Period and search
docs.text:
• Day or Shift sets the period. The same switch is on the bottom bar.
  • Refresh loads the newest deals; Filters narrows the list.
  • Each view has its own search box.

Side in the blotter

The blotter shows the deal from the dealer's side, so a client's buy appears as the dealer's sell (B/S), with the price side in Bid/Ask.

docs.title: Events, History and Exposure
docs.text: Watch how: Events, messages and exposure (0:58)

docs.title: Events and Message
docs.text:
Collects everything the server reports: logins, deals, margin warnings and messages. Click an event to read all of it below the list.

The tab also shows:

  • Price Alerts: your alerts. Add one by right-clicking an instrument in Rates & Charts → Set Price Alert.
  • News: the latest market headlines.
  • STP logs at the bottom: orders passed on to your liquidity providers. Filled ones are on the left and failed ones on the right. Look-back sets how many hours they cover.

Margin warnings also appear briefly at the top right of the screen (for example "Equity has reached 64% of Used Margin").

docs.title: Position History
docs.text: Lists closed positions. Open it for one account from the account's right-click menu → Closed Positions; the title then shows the account, and Show All Accounts goes back to everyone.

docs.title: Symbol Exposure
docs.text: Your net position in each instrument: deals, average price, net lots and exposure, swaps, commissions and profit. TOTAL at the top adds up the whole book. Search to find an instrument; Export CSV saves the table.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
Watch how: Log in to the dealer app (0:40)

Start ActTrader Dealer. The login screen is marked DEALER. Click the Server box and pick your dealing server from the list, then enter your dealer login and password and click Login.

After you log in, the app loads every account, order and position in your book. On a large book this takes a few seconds. Connected next to the logo shows that live updates are flowing.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
Watch how: Find your way around the dealer screen (1:18)

Tabs across the top

  • Accounts: every client account. The Summary under it totals open positions by instrument.
  • Rates & Charts: every instrument with live prices. Here you change prices, spreads and negotiation.
  • Orders: pending orders of all traders. The badge on the tab counts them.
  • Trades: every open position in the book.
  • Blotter: deals done today or this shift, and your result by instrument.
  • Position History: closed positions.
  • Events and Message: server events, price alerts, news and the STP logs.
  • Symbol Exposure: your net exposure in each instrument.

Top right

  • Market Open shows whether trading is open. Clicking it closes trading for every trader, so use it only when you mean to.
  • Dealer: shows your login, and the profile name next to it.
  • Message sends a note to traders. See Messages to Clients.

Icons on the right edge: profiles, theme (dark or light), Price Changer, Order Depth and settings. See Icons and Settings.

Bottom bar: your dealer account, and Day / Shift, which switches the blotter period.

Keyboard

Every grid can be used from the keyboard. In Rates & Charts the keys shown above the grid work on the selected row: R rate, N negotiation, G range, H high/low, I interest, C chart.

docs.title: Icons and Settings
docs.text:
The icons on the right edge of the window, from the top:

Watch how: Icons on the right and Settings (1:07)

Icon What it does Profiles Keeps different screen layouts. Type a name and Create to save the current layout; click a profile to switch to it. Theme Dark or light, and the font size (S, M, L, XL or the slider). Price Changer Sets prices for many instruments at once: select them, move the price with the quick buttons, and Apply. Order Depth Pending orders by price for an instrument: buy on the left, sell on the right. Settings The Settings window (below).

Price Changer's Apply changes the price for every trader

Use Close to leave without changing anything.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Tab What is in it Account Your dealer ID, login and currency; the time zone used for every time in the app (your computer's, the server's, or one you choose); and the currency money values are shown in. Notifications Which events pop up (margin calls, feed problems, equity warnings, rate outside the rate limit and others), and whether to ask for confirmation before you execute, confirm or reject an order. Security Change your password. Session Log out.

docs.title: Pending Orders
docs.text:
The Orders tab lists every pending order in the book: entry orders waiting for their price, and orders waiting for your confirmation. The badge on the tab counts all pending orders, and it updates live.

Watch how: Handle pending orders (1:22)

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column Meaning Order, Account, Instrument, B/S, Lot, Rate The order itself. Proximity Distance from the order rate to the market, in pips. It updates live. Negative means the market has crossed the order rate. T Order type: ES entry stop, EL entry limit, S stop, L limit, I initiate (market), C close. Hover the header for the full list. Time When the order was placed. Trader The trader login. TR Trader range.

More columns (Ticket, OCO, trailing stop, Predef.Stop, Predef.Limit, comment and others) can be turned on: right-click a column header and choose Customize columns….

docs.title: Orders waiting for you
docs.text:
Watch how: Confirm a client order (0:39)

When an account's negotiation needs the dealer (see Account Settings), its orders wait here, highlighted at the top of the list. Type I is a market order to open a position. Proximity shows how far the market has moved from the client's price.

Select the order and press Accept (or right-click → Accept order). Confirm Order shows the order; you can fill it at another rate or for a different amount, or leave them as they are, and press Accept. The order becomes the client's position and leaves the list.

Quick Confirm (Shift+F3), Quick Execute (Shift+F4) and Quick Reject (Shift+F8) act on the selected order without the window.

What Reject does on your server

In ActTrader a dealer reject sends the order back to the client at a price (a re-quote); the quick reject uses the current market price. On the test server, rejecting a waiting market order still opened the client's position at the order's own price. Confirm with your back office how your server handles a rejected order before relying on it.

docs.title: Changing an order
docs.text:
Right-click an order:

  • Modify Order (F8) changes its rate or size. It is available for stop, limit and entry orders that have not triggered yet.
  • Stop, Limit and Trailing Stop (entry orders only) attach a stop-loss or take-profit to the entry order. They apply once the order fills; the entry rate does not change. The window works like the one for an open position, measured from the order's rate. The Predef.Stop / Predef.Limit columns show them.
  • Remove order cancels the order for the client after you confirm; the confirmation names the order. Afterwards no order is selected. An order that has already triggered cannot be removed (unless your server allows it): execute or deactivate it first. A market order waiting for your confirmation (type I) cannot be removed either: accept or reject it.
  • Deactivate Order (also the Deactivate button) is for a stop, limit or entry order that has triggered and is waiting for you. After you confirm, the order goes back to waiting for its price instead of being filled. It is greyed out for any other order.
  • Link OCO Order… links two entry orders as One-Cancels-Other: when one fills, the other is cancelled. Only orders of the same client, instrument and side, one limit and one stop, not yet triggered, can be linked. The OCO column (turn it on with Customize columns…) shows each order's partner. If either order is already linked to a third one, you are warned, and linking replaces that link: the third order is left unlinked.
  • Order Depth shows the instrument's pending orders by price.
Watch how: Link two orders as OCO (0:45)

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
The right-click menu also switches the view: Show Entry, Show Imminent (orders close to triggering) and Show Urgent (orders that need you now).

Row colours: a stop, limit or entry order within the instrument's imminent distance (ImmD on Rates & Charts) has a light amber row; one that has triggered and waits for you has a strong amber row and a filled Proximity cell.

docs.title: Open Positions
docs.text:
The Trades tab lists every open position in the book. Search above the grid by account, instrument or trader to narrow it.

Watch how: Manage a client position (1:14)

Each row shows the instrument, account, lot, side, open and current close price, Stop and Limit, and the profit: Lot P/L (points per lot), P/L (points × lots) and Net P/L (money, after charges, in the account's currency). The grid updates live as prices move and as positions open and close.

docs.title: Managing a position
docs.text:
These act on the client's real position

Right-click a position:

  • Stop sets the stop loss. Type a rate, or a distance in points; the projected loss is shown. The stop appears in the Stop column. Remove in the same window deletes it.
  • Limit sets the take profit the same way; it appears in the Limit column.
  • Trailing Stop sets a stop that follows the price at a fixed distance.
  • Close Position closes it for the client: all of it or part, at the current rate or at a rate you set.
  • Hedge Position and Close with Hedge: see Hedge and Close with Hedge.
  • Show in Trader Details opens the trader's accounts, positions and orders in one window.
  • Trade Audit and Order History open the server's report for the trade in your web browser.

The menu also has Display All Positions, Display Incoming Positions, Hide Selected Positions and Select All Positions to control what the grid shows.

docs.title: Hedge and Close with Hedge
docs.text: Watch how: Hedge and close with hedge (0:47)

docs.title: Hedge Position
docs.text:
Opens the opposite position for the client: a sell against a buy, or a buy against a sell, of the same size or less. Set the amount and the rate (or keep Use current dealing rate), then press Hedge. The new position appears in Trades next to the original one.

Hedge Position is only offered when the client's position in that instrument is not already balanced: when the buys and sells are equal, there is nothing to hedge.

docs.title: Close with Hedge
docs.text:
Closes a position against its opposite one. Both close together, at one rate, and both leave the list.

Both are real trades for the client

The hedge opens a real position, and Close with Hedge closes two.

docs.title: Rates & Charts
docs.text:
Rates & Charts lists every instrument with live bid, ask and spread, the day's high and low, the time of the last price, rollover values and break times.

Watch how: Manage instrument rates (1:32)

Price, negotiation and range changes apply to every trader

Changes made here affect everyone who trades the instrument, as soon as you apply them.

docs.title: The action buttons
docs.text:
Each row has three buttons:

  • Rate opens Change Price: set a new bid or ask, the spread, the feed mode and source, or shift the feed price. The quick buttons move the price by whole pips. Apply sends it to every trader at once.
  • Neg. sets negotiation for the instrument: Auto fills at once; Value and Full need your confirmation.
  • Set Range sets the dealer range, in pips, for the instrument.

Greyed-out rows are inactive instruments.

docs.title: Imminent distance (ImmD)
docs.text:
ImmD is how close, in pips, a pending order must be to the market before the Orders tab marks it as imminent (light amber row, and the Show Imminent view). By default it is the server's value for every instrument. Turn the column on with Customize columns… on the header's right-click menu.

To use your own value for one instrument, select only that row and click its ImmD cell. Untick Default, type the distance (up to two decimals; 0 means only an order at the market price is imminent) and press OK. Tick Default again to go back to the server's value. The setting is yours only: it changes what you see, not the clients' orders.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text: The keys shown above the grid work on the selected row: R rate, N negotiation, G range, H high/low, I interest, C chart, Space select.

docs.title: Right-click menu
docs.text:
Price Changer, View on Chart, Order Depth, Set Price Alert, Set Negotiation, Set Dealer Range, Set High / Low, Set Rollover Interest, selection and Export data to CSV.

  • View on Chart opens a live chart of the instrument in its own window. The dealer chart is for looking only: it has no buy/sell buttons or trading from the chart.
  • Order Depth shows pending orders by price: buy on the left, sell on the right.
